found.summary:
I looked at the sheet and all eight frames at full size, at about 480 px and at the 300 px row tile, and measured them with my own masks. Nothing looks fake and I found no blocking issue.

0.1x matches the owner's words best. It is the same kind of see-through tinted acrylic as the Tropos, nothing white shows anywhere, and the satin edges glow in the speakers' hue: front band Ember L26 C44 h35 and Poison L31 C40 h141, against Tropos hues of about 35 and 140. Poison reads emerald, with no olive left. It is lighter than the speakers: the coloured pixels average C* 35 (Ember) and 31 (Poison) against 55 and 46 on the Tropos, the top reads grey over the base, and Ember's top reads pinker (h23-24).

0.3x is the real alternative. Where the top is lit from below it is about twice as colourful (C* 46-49 against 24-26), but the satin edges go dark: Poison's band is L14 C14, near black in the middle. The README's 'top C* 11 at both' hides this trade, so the owner should be told it plainly.

1x has near-black edges (band L9 C4). Its label 'Speakers' dye' could lead the owner to pick it as the literal 'like the speakers', so the sentence has to say it goes dark.

An in-between strength such as 0.2x was not rendered. It is the frame to make if the owner finds 0.1x too pale on top; I make no claim about how it would look.

Evidence images and scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product/. The ones to open first are tropos-vs-decks-480.png, row-300.png, chroma-03-vs-01.png, ember-frontedge-zoom.png, poison-frontedge-zoom.png and band.py.

verdicts.reasoning: I built my own masks. The front-band mask uses the band's real outline, taken from where the satin and polished frames differ: top y=503+0.2455(x-80), bottom y=529+0.2477(x-80). Top face over the floor: left overhang 0.3x vs 0.1x reads Ember L52 C44 h25 vs L66 C23 h24 (1.9x) and Poison L64 C47 h145 vs L74 C26 h144 (1.8x). The back-right corner over the floor reads Ember C43 vs C22 and Poison C48 vs C26. The strip just behind the front edge (x 100-300) is only 1.4-1.5x: Ember C32 vs C21, Poison C33 vs C23. Satin front band 0.3x vs 0.1x: Ember L15 C27 vs L28 C52 (1.9x); Poison L13 C14 vs L34 C46 (3.3x, more than twice). The top over the dark base stays C7-17 at every loading, and that is what the README's 'C* 11 at both' reflects. So the trade is real and the average hides it. One correction: the critic's band polygon drifts above the band toward the right. 31% of its pixels right of x=380 lie on the top face, and it covers only 61-73% of the band (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/band-mask-check.png). That is why its 0.1x band reads C44/C40 against my C52/C46. The conclusion does not change.

The 1x front band measures L8 C4 in both tints. Pixels with C*>15 over the full frame: 19,125 (Ember) and 15,362 (Poison) at 1x, against 36,005 and 36,685 at 0.1x; the counts match exactly. At my 300 px tiles both 1x decks read dark red with black edges and dark green with black edges (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/row-300-both.png). Two nuances. First, the speakers' own panel edges also read near black on the Tropos tile (vertical edges L0-7 C0-10, 3-4 px wide), so dark edges are what this dye does at this strength. Second, the 1x top over the floor is as close to the Tropos face colour as 0.3x: dE 43 vs 44 for Ember and 27 vs 28 for Poison, with Ember at hue 30, the closest of any loading. So '1x looks least like the speakers' holds for the overall look, not for every part. The real problem with 1x is that its satin edges read black, so the satin the owner asked for cannot be seen. The label or sentence must still say this.

Mean C* of pixels with C*>15: Tropos tile Ember 55.3 and Poison 46.2; 0.1x deck 34.6 and 31.2. The coloured pixels' mean L is higher on the deck (Ember 33.8 vs 25.7, Poison 40.3 vs 29.3), so the deck is both paler and lighter. Top over the base (x 480-560, y 545-575) reads Ember L33 C14 h29 and Poison L37 C15 h141, which looks greyish at 480 px. Front-band hue at 0.1x: Ember 36 and Poison 141. The Tropos's coloured-pixel median is 35.4 and 139.7, and my Tropos face patches read h37-40 and h136-139. In my 3x zooms of the deck's right half I can see the tonearm pillar, the sub-platter arc, the base and the L-shaped inner reflection of the edges through the deck. At 480 px beside the Tropos the 0.1x deck reads as the same see-through tinted acrylic, clearly lighter (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/ember-480-tropos-03-01.png, poison-480-tropos-03-01.png).

0.3x front band on the true outline: Poison L13 C14, middle third L10 C9; Ember L15 C27, middle third L13 C21. In Poison 68% of the band's pixels are below L12, against 0% at 0.1x. At 480 px and in 4x zooms, Poison's 0.3x front edge is a near-black bottle green across its left and middle (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/poison-right-zoom.png). Ember's 0.3x edge is darker but not black: it reads as an even, matte maroon band. So 'barely shows' fits Poison fully and Ember mostly. It supports 0.1x.

Ember top hue where lit from below at 0.1x: overhang L66 C23 h24, strip L35 C21 h24, back-right corner L74 C22 h24. At 0.3x it is h25-26, and at 1x h30. Tropos face patches read h37-40 (mean L42 C84 h39). The deck's own front band at 0.1x is h36. At 480 px beside the scarlet Tropos, the 0.1x top reads as a rose pink-red. Part of the pink comes from the top being light and weak (L66 C23), and part from the hue moving about 15 degrees toward magenta. The hue drifts the same way as the loading drops, so it is the model's prediction for an unmade pour. Checking it on a cast sample is the right step.

Poison 0.1x: 92% of the deck's coloured pixels (C*>8) have hue 128-155 and only 2.2% have hue 95-128. The chroma-weighted mean hue is 141. Front band reads L34 C46 h141, top h143-145, top over the base h141. The Tropos face is h138, with patches h136-139. On the earlier decision sheet the stock-dye Poison decks read olive; here no olive is visible at 300 px or 480 px. It is lighter than the Tropos, as noted: overhang L74 C26 against the Tropos face L46 C68.

Inside the deck outline, shrunk 4 px with the record label left out, near-white pixels (L>70, C<12) number 0-3 in every frame. The rest of the near-white pixels sit on the outline's border or on the studio floor around the base (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/nearwhite-overlay-ember-k0.1.png). Under the deck I see only the dark base and black parts. Glint under the tonearm base at 0.1x: Ember 285 px (x 621-669, y 491-508), mean L73, max L82, C24; Poison 350 px (x 610-669, y 491-509), mean L80, max L93, C27. It is a thin arc of about 50x8 px and reads as a highlight (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/armbase-glint-zoom.png). There Ember reads L74 C22 with pixels up to L80, and Poison L83 C26 with pixels up to L90. It is still clearly tinted glass over the floor, so the conclusion stands.

On the sheet's Tropos tiles (400x500) the cabinet top shows only as a black line 4-5 px tall (L0-8 at y 191-196 for x 150, 200 and 255) under the horn. The camera sees it nearly edge-on (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/tropos-top-zoom.png). verified.pick_check: I keep the pick: 0.1x satin in both tints, with 0.3x beside it. At 0.1x the satin edge is the only part of any deck close to the speakers' colour (front band dE 36 Ember, 25 Poison, against the Tropos face; 0.3x band 64/63). At 0.1x the satin also shows as an even, glowing band, and the owner asked for satin edges. But the trade is not the same in the two tints. For Ember it is even: top over the floor 0.3x C44 vs 0.1x C23, edge 0.1x C52 vs 0.3x C27, about 1.9x each way. The Ember 0.3x top is also much closer to the speaker face (dE 44 vs 67). So under 'deep colour' Ember 0.3x is a real contender. For Poison, 0.1x clearly wins: its edge has 3.3x the chroma of 0.3x, and 68% of the 0.3x Poison band is near black (L<12). Changes to the sentence: (1) 'Every deck here ... with satin edges' is false for the sheet's last column (0.1x polished). Either drop that column from the owner's copy or name it. (2) Tie 1x to his own ask. At the speakers' strength the satin edges turn black (band L8 C4, as dark as the speakers' own panel edges, L0-7), so the satin cannot be seen. That is the reason to drop 1x, not only that it goes dark. (3) Tell him the Ember top looks a little pink beside the speakers (h24 vs h39). (4) Say the custom pour is not yet quoted and the colour will be checked on a cast sample. This follows the 'technically possible' and 'shown truly' rules and the ember-top-pink finding. (5) Use short sentences in place of one 75-word sentence with brackets. Suggested text: "Every deck uses the speakers' own dye, with nothing white under it and satin edges (the last picture has polished edges, to compare). At the speakers' full strength a 25 mm deck goes dark and its satin edges turn black, so the satin can't be seen. At one tenth of that strength the edges glow in the speakers' colour and the top is lighter, like tinted glass; in Ember the top looks a little pink. At three tenths the top is deeper but the edges are dark, nearly black in Poison. We suggest one tenth. It needs a custom pour that isn't quoted yet, and we'd check the colour on a sample first." No loading between 0.1x and 0.3x was rendered. If the owner wants a deeper Ember top with glowing edges, rendering one is the only way to see whether it gives both. Evidence and scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b65/critic-product-verify/ (masks.py, vlab.py, row-300-both.png, ember-480-tropos-03-01.png, poison-480-tropos-03-01.png, ember-leftoverhang-4load.png, poison-leftoverhang-4load.png, band-mask-check.png).

findings.frame: README line 'Satin edges carry the colour better than polished' and sheet column 5 (ember-k0.1-polished-edge.png, poison-k0.1-polished-edge.png)
findings.what: 'About twice the colour' holds only on the left half of the long front face, where the posts and phono box sit behind a polished edge, and on the short right face. On the right half of the front face, polished carries the same colour as satin. Over the whole front face the gap is about 15% by Lab mean, and none by linear-light mean. The physics: a polished edge is a window down the deck's length. It shows deep colour where the long path ends on the bright backdrop and goes dark where it meets the posts and holes. Satin blurs that into one even band. So the README's 'reflects most of it back inside and shows the interior' is only half right. A plain line that matches the frames: 'Satin spreads the colour evenly round the edge; polished shows it in patches, with the posts showing through, and its short sides go grey.'

Front face, left half (x 100-312): Ember 45.6 vs 29.8, Poison 42.0 vs 27.2, which reproduces the lane's 46/26 and 42/22. Front face, right half (x 312-525): Ember 59.0 vs 59.0, Poison 51.3 vs 52.0. Whole front face: 52.5 vs 45.0 and 46.8 vs 40.1 (linear-light mean 53.5 vs 55.0 and 47.6 vs 49.0). Short right face: 25.5 vs 12.0 and 22.6 vs 10.2. Along the polished front face, 53-px segments run from C* 9 to 74 (Ember) and 8 to 65 (Poison). Visible at 480 px in critic-photo/pair480-ember.png and pair480-poison.png.

findings.frame: README table 'Top' column and the lines 'The top cannot match the Tropos front ... C* 5-11' and 'Lighter dye does not raise the top past C* 11'
findings.what: The lane's top numbers come from the strip in front of the platter, over the black base, and they reproduce there. Where the floor shows up through the deck (the overhangs), the top is much stronger: 0.3x is close to the Tropos, 0.1x is about half of that, and at 0.1x Ember turns pink (hue 24 against the Tropos's 36). The physics is sound (Beer-Lambert): the long edge path favours light dye and the short top path favours heavier dye. But the sheet should show this as a trade: 0.1x gives edges near the speakers and a pale top; 0.3x gives a top near the speakers where light comes through, with dark edges. You can see it in the 300 px row: 0.3x reads as a coloured deck, 0.1x as pale glass with a coloured rim. 'The top can't' is not true for the whole top.

found.summary:
Nothing reads as CG at 480 px or at full size. The satin bands change smoothly with the light behind them, the 1 px chamfer reads as a machined arris, and the polished top behaves as real acrylic over a dark interior.

**My numbers against the lane's:**
- **Edges:** I reproduce the lane's figures only on the left half of the front face (Ember 45.6, Poison 42.0). Over the whole front face satin reads 52.5 and 46.8; on the short right face 25.5 and 22.6.
